title: HRSA HPSA component categories condition the interpretation of modeled county social need
source_unit: US county with current designated primary-care HPSA component/type/population codes and 2025 CDC PLACES modeled county estimates
geography: United States; 2,685 matched counties with at least one designated primary-care HPSA row and selected PLACES measures

observations.period: 2025 PLACES; counties with geographic HPSA type

denominator.unit: matched counties containing Hpsa Geo or Hpsa Geo HN type

lack_health_insurance.unit: median PLACES percent of adults aged 18-64

observations.method: County FIPS association; unweighted medians; groups overlap.
observations.uncertainty: Geographic HPSA type does not show component boundaries, reachability, quality, or resident-level exposure; PLACES is modeled.
observations.counterinterpretation: County composition, neighboring access, and designation selection may explain differences.

observations.period: 2025 PLACES; counties with population HPSA type

denominator.unit: matched counties containing Hpsa Pop type

lack_health_insurance.unit: median PLACES percent of adults aged 18-64

observations.method: County FIPS association; unweighted medians; groups overlap.
observations.uncertainty: Population designation is not equivalent to the PLACES county adult denominator; designated population identity and local access remain unmeasured.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher county medians may reflect the designated population, broader county composition, or selection rather than a population-specific care effect.

observations.period: 2025 PLACES; counties with low-income HPSA population code

denominator.unit: matched counties with LI, LI-MFW, or LI-H-MFW HPSA population code

lack_health_insurance.unit: median PLACES percent of adults aged 18-64

observations.method: County FIPS association; unweighted medians; groups overlap.
observations.uncertainty: The HPSA code does not identify all low-income residents or make PLACES a designated-population estimate.
observations.subgroup: Counties with low-income HPSA population codes.
observations.counterinterpretation: The pattern may reflect county resources, composition, rurality, insurance, or designation targeting rather than a shortage effect.

observations.period: 2025 PLACES; counties with migrant or seasonal HPSA population code

denominator.unit: matched counties with M, MFW, LI-MFW, or LI-H-MFW HPSA population code

lack_health_insurance.unit: median PLACES percent of adults aged 18-64

observations.method: County FIPS association; unweighted medians; groups overlap.
observations.uncertainty: This is a small, selected county group and PLACES county medians do not identify migrant/seasonal residents.
observations.subgroup: Counties with migrant or seasonal HPSA population codes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower modeled medians may reflect geography, composition, selection, neighboring access, or denominator mismatch; they do not imply better care.

related_sources.claim: Reproduction output for HPSA component-conditioned medians.

boundary: This is an overlapping ecological diagnostic. HRSA component and population categories are not mutually exclusive county treatments; PLACES estimates are modeled county averages. The record does not establish resident-level shortage, provider adequacy, causal effects, patient use, household burden, trust, or political action.
